I'm about 8 months in, still on the practice chanter, working out of the green tutor. I'm a lvl 2 student. We are working on the technical aspects now, grips, tachums, doublings, taoluaths, and such. We don't get actual pipes till level 4. There's a band here in my town that plays consistently, and the offer lessons.

Apparently, I was a bit over served one night and decided I needed to learn to play the bagpipes. A few days later a chanter showed up via UPS and so I figured I better find someone to show me how to play them.

Haha, awesome. I was sober when I ordered mine, but I'd recently found a love of single malt scotches and been to a local Scottish Games & Ceilidh. I'm just taking private instruction right now, but there is a band I will probably join after I get my pipes and figure out how to work them :P

The tutor I'm using was put together by the guy who taught my teacher, so I don't know how different it is. I haven't gotten to grips and taoluaths yet, but I've just started doublings and birls.

Doublings killed me, we had to star low and go high, then start high and go low, all with a gracenotes leading the base note. The slight difference with the High A and G kicked my butt.

Birls should be easy, but I have a trick pinky that makes brushing that low G somewhat jankey. I'll dial it in though.

I've been just tapping on the birls so far, I don't trust my ring finger enough to try sliding my pinkie. I'll probably have to figure out how to do that soon so I can be faster, but I'm still having a hard time not strangling the chanter and it makes that sort of thing harder.
Work on that ring finger, you'll need a B gracenote for a taoluath on D.
